subject: design-technology
title: Lifecycle Analysis (LCA)
welcome_lead: Cradle to grave — accounting for every stage.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: LCA, cradle-to-grave, and ISO 14040.

concepts.def: Life Cycle Assessment — quantifying environmental impacts across a product's life.
Accounting from raw material extraction to end-of-life disposal.
LCA stage cataloguing inputs (energy, materials) and outputs (emissions).
Quantified function used to compare alternatives (e.g. 1 km driven).

walkthroughs.body_html: ISO 14040 (first published 1997, revised 2006) sets out four LCA stages: goal and scope, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation.
A meaningful LCA compares like with like via a functional unit: '1 km transported', '1 L pasteurised milk packaged'. Without it, comparisons mislead.
Outputs include Global Warming Potential (kg CO2e), acidification (kg SO2e), eutrophication (kg PO4e), water use, and resource depletion. Trade-offs are common.

mcqs.q: How many main LCA stages does ISO 14040 define?

numericals.q: If a product emits 25 kg CO2e in use and 5 kg in production, use phase is what % of total?
